hints.title: Horizontal Level Grouping
hints.text: Group points sharing the same vertical coordinate to count available endpoints per horizontal line.

hints.title: Segment Combinatorics per Level
hints.text: For each level with c points, the number of candidate horizontal bases is c * (c - 1) / 2.

hints.title: Pairwise Level Multiplication
hints.text: Combine pairs of bases from distinct levels using a running sum accumulator.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def countTrapezoids(self, points: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        # Group points by y coordinate
        y_counts = Counter(y for x, y in points)
        # For each y, number of horizontal segments is c*(c-1)//2
        seg_counts = [c * (c - 1) // 2 for c in y_counts.values() if c >= 2]
        
        # A trapezoid is formed by choosing 1 segment from y1 and 1 segment from y2 (y1 != y2)
        # Sum of seg[i] * seg[j] for i < j
        total = 0
        running_sum = 0
        for cnt in seg_counts:
            total += running_sum * cnt
            running_sum += cnt
            
        return total
```

variables: U: number of unique y coordinates
complexity.notes: Linear coordinate frequency grouping and running sum multiplication.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all point quadruplets requires O(N^4) operations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Frequency map collapses points into levels in linear memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use combinatorial selection on horizontal line levels.
